events.objective: Establish the true symptom onset and blast radius. Query logs and metrics for order-service, market-data-service, and pricing-engine between 2026-05-20T11:00:00Z and 2026-05-20T13:59:00Z. Determine: (1) exact time quote timeouts began and whether it precedes or follows the market-data-service deploy; (2) whether pricing-engine p99 2.6s is a new regression or pre-existing, and its onset time; (3) the specific error signatures/timeout messages on order-service (which downstream call is timing out); (4) whether other services calling pricing-engine or market-data-service are also affected; (5) resource trends (CPU, memory, GC, connection/thread pool saturation) on pricing-engine and order-service over the window. Report the earliest affected component and exact onset timestamp.

Map what changed and what depends on what, across ALL services. Retrieve deployments and config changes between 2026-05-20T10:00:00Z and 2026-05-20T13:59:00Z (with timestamps) for order-service, market-data-service, pricing-engine, and any service order-service depends on. Retrieve service dependencies to identify shared components (datastore, cache, queue, message bus) between pricing-engine and market-data-service, and what order-service's quote path actually calls. Search historical incidents for prior quote-timeout or serialization-change incidents and their resolutions.

Correlate the change timeline against the onset time established in task a. Identify whether the market-data-service serialization change, or any other deployment/config change, landed immediately before the onset timestamp, and whether any change touched a shared dependency of pricing-engine. Assess whether the market-data-service change is causally positioned to cause pricing-engine p99 latency, or whether timing points to a different change or an untracked/shared-resource fault. Provide a ranked list of candidate root causes with supporting/contradicting evidence.

events.statement: Only one deployment in 10:00–13:59Z across ALL services: dep-6111, market-data-service v5.2.0, deployed 2026-05-20T11:56:00Z by v.rao, 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf' ('protobuf quote payloads for internal callers'), status 'live', rolled_back_at null. No deployment on order-service, pricing-engine, or any other service in the window.

Two config changes in the window (full, non-partial retry): cfg-3118 api-gateway 'ratelimit.burst' 200→250 at 2026-05-20T10:30:00Z (config-bot), and cfg-3120 pricing-engine 'flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct' 5→100 at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z by 'pm-experiments' ('Ramp Greeks v2 experiment to all traffic'). The pricing-engine flag ramp at 12:04Z is ~8 minutes after the protobuf deploy.

order-service's quote path (dependency edges, caller→callee) is: api-gateway → order-service → {pricing-engine (http), ledger-db (db), exchange-gateway (http), kafka (queue-produce)}; pricing-engine → {market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache)}. So order-service does NOT call market-data-service directly — it goes through pricing-engine. market-data-service → redis-cache (cache) and → exchange-gateway (http).

redis-cache is the only shared component connecting pricing-engine and market-data-service: both have edges to redis-cache (kind 'cache'), and redis-cache is flagged shared=true, owner platform. So a shared cache is a possible cross-service path from the market-data serialization change to pricing-engine latency, independent of the direct pricing-engine→market-data-service http edge.

Other shared platform components in the graph: ledger-db (postgres, shared=true, used by order-service) and kafka (kafka, shared=true, order-service produces to it). These — plus redis-cache — are shared components that could transmit faults from a neighbour into order-service or pricing-engine.

Historical leads (search 'quote timeout serialization change'): HIST-107 (2025-12-09) 'Cold cache storm after redis failover', services redis-cache + market-data-service, symptoms cache miss storm / quote latency, root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', resolution warmed cache + fixed replica sync checks; and HIST-113 (2026-01-28) 'pricing-engine CPU saturation at market open', symptom quote timeouts + cpu 99%, root cause capacity saturation, resolution raised replica count. Both are leads only, not evidence about the current incident; note neither prior incident was caused by a serialization/deploy change, and both implicate redis-cache or pricing-engine capacity rather than market-data's protobuf change.

events.answer: Across all services in 10:00–13:59Z there was exactly one deployment — market-data-service v5.2.0 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf', dep-6111 at 11:56:00Z, still live and NOT rolled back — plus two config changes: api-gateway ratelimit.burst 200→250 at 10:30Z, and pricing-engine flag flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5→100 at 12:04:00Z (pm-experiments). Dependency map: api-gateway → order-service → {pricing-engine http, ledger-db, exchange-gateway, kafka}; pricing-engine → {market-data-service http, redis-cache}; order-service has no direct edge to market-data-service. The only shared component linking pricing-engine and market-data-service is redis-cache (shared=true, platform-owned); ledger-db and kafka are the other shared components touching order-service. Historical leads HIST-107 (redis failover cold-cache storm, market-data-service) and HIST-113 (pricing-engine CPU saturation) both differ in cause from a serialization change and are leads only.

events.statement: The earliest anomaly is on pricing-engine: first slow-calc log 'GreeksV2Calculator: Monte-Carlo paths=20000 took 6465ms' at 2026-05-20T12:05:21Z, immediately preceded by config change 'config change cfg-3120 applied: flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100' at 12:04:16Z.

order-service quote timeouts begin at 2026-05-20T12:06:10Z, AFTER pricing-engine's first slow calc (12:05:21Z): 225 ERROR log lines of the single pattern 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after <n>ms orderId=<n>', first seen 12:06:10Z.

pricing-engine p99 latency was flat ~58-62ms all morning through the 11:56-11:59 buckets, then jumped to avg 2489ms in the bucket starting 12:05:00Z and stayed ~2,500-2,850ms through 13:56Z — a new regression coinciding with the 12:04:16 config change, not pre-existing.

market-data-service deployed dep-6111 (v5.2.0) at 2026-05-20T11:56:45Z but shows no errors and stays responsive afterward ('served batch of requests, p50=393ms' at 12:01:29Z); its only WARN is an unrelated 'deprecated TLS cipher offered by client' at 11:43:53Z — it is not the earliest-affected component.

order-service error_rate jumped from a ~0.17-0.25% baseline (11:00-11:56) to 6.08% in the bucket starting 12:04:00Z and ~8.1-8.4% thereafter, a blast-radius confirmation at the same onset window as pricing-engine.

pricing-engine's own error signature is 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2' (276 occurrences, first at 12:06:41Z), i.e. the GreeksV2 calculator exceeds its internal budget, while order-service's downstream timeout threshold is 2500ms — the pricing-engine failure precedes and causes the order-service timeouts.

events.answer: Quote timeouts began at ~12:05–12:06 on 2026-05-20, driven by pricing-engine's quote computation (GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator), NOT by the market-data-service deploy. pricing-engine p99 jumped from ~60ms (stable all morning) to ~2,500–2,850ms in the bucket starting 12:05:00, exactly after the config change cfg-3120 which set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100 at 12:04:16. market-data-service deployed dep-6111 at 11:56:45 and its own logs remain healthy (served batches at p50=393ms at 12:01:29), so it is not the earliest-affected component. The earliest affected component is pricing-engine, with first symptom at 12:05:21; order-service is a downstream victim whose timeouts start at 12:06:10. Whether other callers of pricing-engine are also affected could not be checked (budget).

args.query: protobuf serialization change latency regression downstream

events.statement: Full re-query of deployments 10:00–13:59Z across all services returned exactly one: dep-6111 market-data-service v5.2.0 at 11:56:00Z, status live, rolled_back_at null. A second, narrower query scoped to service=pricing-engine for 11:30–12:06:30Z returned count 0 deployments, so nothing was deployed to pricing-engine (or its own stack) near the 12:05 onset.

A tight-window config query (11:40–12:10Z) returned exactly one change: cfg-3120, pricing-engine, key flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct old_value 5 → new_value 100, changed_at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z, author pm-experiments, 'Ramp Greeks v2 experiment to all traffic'. This is the only change in the ~5 minutes before the 12:05:21Z first slow calc, and it directly alters the pricing-engine calculator named in the slow-calc log.

Dependency re-query confirms order-service reaches market-data-service only indirectly: order-service → pricing-engine (http) → market-data-service (http). market-data-service and pricing-engine both have edges to redis-cache (kind 'cache'), and redis-cache is flagged type 'redis', owner platform, shared=true. So redis-cache is the single shared component (other than the direct http edge) through which market-data-service could affect pricing-engine.

config-change queries scoped to redis-cache and to market-data-service for 11:00–13:59Z each returned count 0: no config change touched the shared cache or market-data-service in the window. Hence no tracked change landed on the shared dependency (redis-cache) of pricing-engine at any point around onset.

redis-cache is shared by a wider set than pricing-engine/market-data-service: auth-service and portfolio-service also have cache edges to it, and api-gateway and portfolio-service call market-data-service over http. If the shared cache were the fault vector, those extra callers are additional exposed neighbours that were not checked in this task.

Historical precedent search gives mixed leads, none matching a serialization change: HIST-107 (2025-12-09) red-cache/market-data-service cold-cache storm (redis primary failure promoted an empty replica) and two bad_deployment precedents HIST-101 (bcrypt cost 10→14) and HIST-109 (JWT clock-skew default) where a config/code value change released at rollout caused the latency — the latter pattern (HIST-101) structurally resembles a flag ramp that makes an expensive code path serve all traffic.

events.description: No metric query was run against redis-cache (or any shared datastore) to look for cache miss rate, evictions, latency or connection saturation around 12:04–12:06Z. The available_metrics list for the redis component type was never retrieved.
Deployment/config searches are limited to registered change records; there is no query for untracked cluster events (node restarts, infra maintenance, autoscaling).
No rollout history for cfg-3120 beyond its application (e.g. whether 5%→100% is the first ramp, or whether a canary at 5% already showed latency).

events.answer: The market-data-service serialization change (dep-6111, 11:56:00Z) is NOT causally positioned at the onset: pricing-engine's p99 regression and first slow GreeksV2 calc start ~9 minutes later, immediately after the pricing-engine config change cfg-3120 (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5→100, 12:04Z). The only change that landed immediately before onset and that directly alters pricing-engine's behavior is cfg-3120. No deployment touched any shared dependency of pricing-engine; the only plausible change-borne shared-resource path is redis-cache, but no config/deploy change touched redis-cache either, so an untracked/shared-resource fault cannot be ruled out but has no supporting change evidence. Ranked candidates: (1) cfg-3120 flag ramp to 100% GreeksV2; (2) untracked shared-resource fault (redis-cache degradation, no tracked change); (3) market-data-service protobuf deploy (timing + healthy downstream argue against).

events.title: GreeksV2 flag ramp (cfg-3120) made an expensive calculator serve all traffic, saturating pricing-engine
market-data-service protobuf deploy dep-6111 (reporter's suspicion) broke quote payloads downstream
Shared redis-cache fault degraded independently, propagating to pricing-engine and market-data-service
Resource saturation (CPU/memory/thread-pool) on pricing-engine or order-service

tasks.answer: Quote timeouts began at ~12:05–12:06 on 2026-05-20, driven by pricing-engine's quote computation (GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator), NOT by the market-data-service deploy. pricing-engine p99 jumped from ~60ms (stable all morning) to ~2,500–2,850ms in the bucket starting 12:05:00, exactly after the config change cfg-3120 which set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100 at 12:04:16. market-data-service deployed dep-6111 at 11:56:45 and its own logs remain healthy (served batches at p50=393ms at 12:01:29), so it is not the earliest-affected component. The earliest affected component is pricing-engine, with first symptom at 12:05:21; order-service is a downstream victim whose timeouts start at 12:06:10. Whether other callers of pricing-engine are also affected could not be checked (budget).
